data.description:
## Context / Problem

The three surface stories (CLI / MCP / library) each need the **same** decision: given a
ticket's current state and the acting session, should we warn that a *different* active
session holds this ticket? Duplicating that logic three ways would drift. This story
provides one **pure** detector plus the config toggle that gates it, so the surfaces only
render.

Ownership is the *live* `claimed_session` (guaranteed live-only by the sibling reducer
story). The acting session id comes from the existing shared resolver
`resolve_session_id()` (`src/rebar/_commands/session_id.py:71`), which returns the first
non-empty of `REBAR_SESSION_ID -> CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID -> OPENCODE_SESSION_ID ->
SESSION_ID`, else `None`. Per the brainstorm decision, when the acting id is `None` we
stay **silent** (we cannot prove we are a *different* session; the un-shimmed case is
common — `docs/session-id-shims.md` gotcha G1), and a default-on config toggle lets an
operator disable the warning if the resume/fork false positives prove noisy.

## Approach

Add a new leaf module `src/rebar/_commands/cross_session.py` with a **pure** function:

```
def cross_session_warning(
    state: Mapping[str, Any], *, acting_session: str | None, enabled: bool
) -> str | None
```

Return `None` (silent) when any of: `enabled` is false; `acting_session` is falsy;
`state.get("claimed_session")` is falsy; or `acting_session == state["claimed_session"]`.
Otherwise return a single-line warning string naming the holder — the `claimed_session`
id, and the `claim_harness` in parentheses when present — e.g.
`ticket held by another session <sid> (harness <tag>)`. The function performs **no** I/O
(no state load, no config read, no env read) so it is trivially unit-testable and reused
verbatim by all three surfaces.

Add a thin convenience `cross_session_warning_for(ticket_id, *, tracker, repo_root)` that
composes the pure function with the real reads: load compiled state (via the same read
path `show`/`ready` use), `resolve_session_id()`, and the config toggle. The surfaces call
this convenience; unit tests target the pure core.

Add the config key `warnings.cross_session` (bool, **default `True`**) to the typed core
schema following the existing `_documented(...)` dataclass-field pattern
(`src/rebar/_config_schema.py:50`) in a new `[warnings]` section registered in
`rebar._config_sections._SECTIONS` (the section registry consumed by
`_config_schema.py:32`). Read it through the composed `Config` (the same load path every
other typed key uses), so it honours `rebar.toml` + env + CLI overrides with no new read
mechanism. The feature is fully **in-process** — no CI provider, no network — satisfying
`project.portability`.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_commands/cross_session.py` — **new** module: the pure `cross_session_warning`
  + the `cross_session_warning_for` convenience.
- `src/rebar/_config_schema.py` — add the `[warnings]` section dataclass with
  `cross_session: bool = _documented(True, ...)`.
- `src/rebar/_config_sections.py` — register the `warnings` section in `_SECTIONS`.
- `docs/config-reference.md` — document `warnings.cross_session` (default true) **and**
  the deliberate silent-when-acting-id-unknown behavior as an evidence-revisitable choice.

## Testing

Tier: **in-process unit test** — the pure detector is a validation-branch function
(test-design §3), and the toggle is exercised through the **real config read path**
(test-design §6 "config-effect contrast"), not a stubbed lookup.

- Truth matrix over the pure `cross_session_warning`: warns (non-None, names holder)
  exactly when `enabled and acting_session and claimed_session and acting_session !=
  claimed_session`; silent (None) for each of the four suppression cases
  (disabled / acting `None` / `claimed_session` absent / equal ids). Parameterized.
- Message content: with `claim_harness` present the string includes both the id and the
  harness tag; without it, just the id.
- Config-effect contrast (real read path): construct a `Config` from a mapping with
  `[warnings] cross_session=false` and one at the default (true); run
  `cross_session_warning_for` against a fixture ticket held by session A while acting as
  B, and assert the default warns and the `false` value is silent — proving the key is
  wired through the actual `Config` load, not just parsed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `cross_session_warning(state, acting_session=..., enabled=...)` returns a non-`None`
  string containing the holder's `claimed_session` id exactly when
  `enabled and acting_session and state["claimed_session"] and acting_session !=
  state["claimed_session"]` (checked by a parameterized unit test matrix under
  `make test`).
- [ ] The detector returns `None` for every suppression case — `enabled=False`,
  `acting_session=None`, `claimed_session` absent/falsy, or equal ids (checked by the same
  parameterized test).
- [ ] The returned string includes the `claim_harness` tag when present and omits it when
  absent (checked by two assertions in a message-content test).
- [ ] Config-effect: with `[warnings] cross_session=false` loaded through the real
  `Config`, `cross_session_warning_for` is silent for an A-held ticket acted on by B; at
  the default it warns (checked by `test_cross_session_config_toggle` exercising the real
  config read path).
- [ ] `docs/config-reference.md` documents `warnings.cross_session` (default true) and the
  silent-when-acting-id-unknown revisitable decision (checked: `grep -n "cross_session"
  docs/config-reference.md` matches, and the note contains "revisit").
data.title: Cross-session warning detector + warnings.cross_session config toggle
